children: Oracle Corporation (NYSE:ORCL) posted strong AI-driven cloud growth and margins but faces rising debt scrutiny after arranging ~$18B for Project Jupiter AI capacity, near-term cash drain and layoffs, a canceled Larry Ellison share sale and local opposition as investor day looms.
Previous Week Recap
Oracle Revenue Highlights And Margin
: Oracle (ORCL) Q1 revenue $19.3B (+30% YoY); cloud infra $7.4B (+121%) driven by AI compute. Adjusted op margin 42%, EPS $1.92 (+31%). Remaining performance obligation $664B.
ORCL OpenAI Data Center Financing
: Oracle (ORCL) arranged $18 billion in loans late last year to build a data center for its OpenAI partnership, funding dedicated AI compute capacity tied to the collaboration.
S&P Cut, Oracle Debt Scrutiny
: Oracle (ORCL) was cut by S&P in July to one notch above junk. Banks are holding more Oracle-linked project debt than planned, increasing scrutiny of ORCL’s total debt.
Ellison Share Sale Plan Scrapped
: ORCL fell ~3.7% after co-founder Larry Ellison scrapped a plan to sell up to 50M shares (~$7.5B). No shares were sold and no reason for the cancellation was given.
Doña Ana Project Jupiter Loans
: Loans tied to Oracle's (ORCL) Doña Ana data‑center lease (Project Jupiter) — about $18B — are quoted near 89–91¢ on the dollar in secondary markets by syndicate banks.
Negative Free Cash Flow
: Oracle (ORCL) posted nearly $5B negative free cash flow; depreciation, capex and restructuring costs cut liquidity during the period.
Project Jupiter Local Opposition
: Oracle (ORCL) faces local opposition over Project Jupiter AI build, citing potential water supply and air quality impacts that could threaten the expansion.
Investor Day And Targets
: Oracle (ORCL) will host investor day Oct 28; Mizuho expects updated long‑term targets, multi‑year margin path, funding plan and possible free‑cash‑flow inflection timing.
Job Cuts And Shares Dip
: Oracle (ORCL) began another round of layoffs, notifying employees this week. Prior cuts removed ~21,000 roles; some teams now face double‑digit percentage reductions. Shares fell ~1.5% premarket.
Top Bidder For Japan Cloud
: Oracle (ORCL) is reported as the top bidder for a Japanese sovereign cloud contract to build air‑gapped infrastructure for sensitive government data; Japan’s final decision is pending.
